nodes.label: ADR-001: No build step; ship pinned CDN ES modules
nodes.rationale: No npm/bundler/package.json; Three.js pinned to three@0.160.0 via a CDN import map, relative paths, explicit .js extensions. Self-contained payloads must run with zero toolchain, work offline after first fetch, stay reproducible; rejected Vite/Webpack, @latest, and the UMD global. ES modules require HTTP (file:// fails); local serving is XAMPP Apache on port 8080.
nodes.norm_label: adr-001: no build step; ship pinned cdn es modules

nodes.label: ADR-002: Host integration via a window.simAPI global, not postMessage
nodes.rationale: Sim runs in a sandboxed iframe exposing window.simAPI (pause/resume/reset) plus a static four-field meta.json; deliberately no postMessage/window.parent/window.top. Smallest possible contract, no async plumbing; in-sim Reset must route through simAPI.reset() (one reset path only).
nodes.norm_label: adr-002: host integration via a window.simapi global, not postmessage

nodes.label: ADR-003: CSS design tokens are the single runtime source of truth for all visual values
nodes.rationale: Every colour/radius/spacing is a CSS custom property read live at runtime via getComputedStyle; no hex literals in JS or component CSS. One visual language across subjects; a re-theme is a token swap; enforces the named rules at a single chokepoint.
nodes.norm_label: adr-003: css design tokens are the single runtime source of truth for all visual values

nodes.label: ADR-004: Every geometry change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline
nodes.rationale: A single rebuild(shapeData) in fixed order (dispose -> resolve angles -> generate mesh -> seat -> analyze edges -> draw projections -> place labels -> notify) is the only geometry path. Prevents WebGL context exhaustion/leaks in the iframe and guarantees consistent state; the orchestrator that owns it grows large.
nodes.norm_label: adr-004: every geometry change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline

nodes.label: ADR-005: Re-derive every ported sign visually (Unity LH -> Three.js RH), explicit ZXY Euler
nodes.rationale: Magnitudes port unchanged but every sign is re-derived visually against a worked square-pyramid; Euler order pinned ZXY (Unity's) in iShape.applyShapeTransform. Copying Unity's negative signs verbatim yields plausible-but-wrong mirrored/back-to-front projections; Three.js default XYZ would silently change rotations.
nodes.norm_label: adr-005: re-derive every ported sign visually (unity lh -> three.js rh), explicit zxy euler

nodes.label: ADR-006: Fat lines + hard-edge geometry + quantized edge welding for crisp technical linework
nodes.rationale: Linework uses LineMaterial + LineSegments2/Line2 fat lines, hard-edged non-indexed geometry, and meshAnalyzer welds endpoints at 1e-3 tolerance. LineBasicMaterial caps at 1px on most GPUs; welding stops double lines on curved-solid rims. Requires resolution sync, computeLineDistances(), and polygonOffset.
nodes.norm_label: adr-006: fat lines + hard-edge geometry + quantized edge welding for crisp technical linework

nodes.label: ADR-007: Orchestrator + leaf modules; leaves don't cross-import, only genericSolid is shared
nodes.rationale: Module 2 is one orchestrator (main.js) owning scene/state/rebuild plus single-purpose leaf modules that do not import each other; only genericSolid.js (stateless polygon trig) may be imported by siblings. Keeps the dependency graph a star so a leaf can be replaced without tracing sibling webs; the orchestrator absorbs all wiring and grows large.
nodes.norm_label: adr-007: orchestrator + leaf modules; leaves don't cross-import, only genericsolid is shared

nodes.label: ADR-008: Rotation priority hierarchy enforced through mutually-exclusive UI
nodes.rationale: Precedence Face-Inclination HP/VP > Orient-to-Corner/Edge preset > Manual Y, a higher mode disabling the lower via uiManager toggles. Prevents contradictory orientation and teaches concepts in order; preset angles are square 45, triangular 30, pentagonal 54 (not 18), hexagonal 30.
nodes.norm_label: adr-008: rotation priority hierarchy enforced through mutually-exclusive ui

nodes.label: ADR-009: No shared code library; topic clones are manual full copies simplified from Module 2 (the master)
nodes.rationale: No shared library or sync tooling; Module 2 is the master and each graphics_module_2_topic_* folder is a full copy simplified via a single ENABLED_TIERS flag. Improvements are backported as merges, not blind copies. Keeps each topic a standalone deployable payload; the copies WILL drift (the deliberate cost).
nodes.norm_label: adr-009: no shared code library; topic clones are manual full copies simplified from module 2 (the master)

nodes.label: ADR-010: DESIGN.shared.md is the platform-wide visual contract, duplicated per module (interim)
nodes.rationale: The platform visual system was extracted into DESIGN.shared.md, meant byte-identical per module with only a module-local appendix. Per-module duplication accepted only as interim because no shared Simatrix root existed yet. Superseded by ADR-022 once the root existed and the copies had drifted.
nodes.norm_label: adr-010: design.shared.md is the platform-wide visual contract, duplicated per module (interim)

nodes.label: ADR-011: Module 1 uses a shared engine.js + thin pages, a different architecture from Module 2
nodes.rationale: Module 1 shipped seven thin HTML pages calling one shared engine (src/engine.js, initSim) over shared shell.css, structurally different from Module 2's orchestrator + leaf modules. Fit its simpler 2D points/lines geometry and stopped the seven pages from drifting. Fully superseded by ADR-033 (partially first by ADR-029).
nodes.norm_label: adr-011: module 1 uses a shared engine.js + thin pages, a different architecture from module 2

nodes.label: ADR-012: On-demand Compare View replaced the persistent dual-pane (PiP + toggle bar + swap())
nodes.rationale: Points/Lines dropped the persistent PiP dual-pane; the main pane is always the live 3D scene (#c3d) and the second view appears on demand in a floating Compare card showing a live-rebuilt (never snapshot) view. swap()/isMain3D() survive as no-op shims. Introduces the no-transform invariant on #sim-viewport/#canvas-area/body.
nodes.norm_label: adr-012: on-demand compare view replaced the persistent dual-pane (pip + toggle bar + swap())

nodes.label: ADR-013: The fold camera moves, overturning 'camera never moves during the fold' (then revised)
nodes.rationale: Overturned the old hard rule; the fold now animates the camera. First replacement (perspective->ortho front-on morph) was replaced by a held-angle dolly (animateFoldHold), which read as a bottom-right swoop and hid the hinge. The held-angle revision is itself fully overturned by ADR-036; the first reversal (camera does move) still stands and must not be re-cited as 'camera never moves'.
nodes.norm_label: adr-013: the fold camera moves, overturning 'camera never moves during the fold' (then revised)

nodes.label: ADR-014: Auto-zoom is a one-shot eased dolly; a rebuild does tight-fit XOR push-back, never both
nodes.rationale: Ported Module 2's clip-aware auto-zoom (reframeIfClipped at end of rebuild, push-back only): a per-rebuild one-shot fixed-duration eased dolly, and a rebuild does either a fresh tight fit (boot/reset) or the push-back (slider edits), never both. Replaced a per-frame exponential follow that lurched; needs an accurate contentBox, not the full grid.
nodes.norm_label: adr-014: auto-zoom is a one-shot eased dolly; a rebuild does tight-fit xor push-back, never both

nodes.label: ADR-015: Self-check is +/-0.5-tolerant, never auto-fills, OR-arrays only for degenerate cases
nodes.rationale: The Problem Library self-check compares dialed values to a target with +/-0.5 tolerance and never auto-fills (loading a problem resets to defaults; the student dials, the check lights green). OR-array targets are allowed only for genuinely degenerate geometry. theta=+/-theta and endpoint A/B ORs were rejected as false positives that green a wrong drawing.
nodes.norm_label: adr-015: self-check is +/-0.5-tolerant, never auto-fills, or-arrays only for degenerate cases

nodes.label: ADR-016: Drawing line conventions follow N.D. Bhatt / ISO
nodes.rationale: Foot/point markers are thick filled dots (paper halo + colour disc); 2D orthographic projectors are solid Type-B continuous thin; 3D pictorial projectors stay dashed. Corrected an earlier 45-degree x foot and solid-VP-in-3D choice. In 2D the HP/VP distinction is carried by position, so solid is standards-correct (N.D. Bhatt); 3D keeps the Two-Cue Rule (HP solid-teal / VP dashed-amber).
nodes.norm_label: adr-016: drawing line conventions follow n.d. bhatt / iso

nodes.label: ADR-017: The Lines sim is a 5-step problem-solving stepper, not six fixed-orientation cases
nodes.rationale: Restructured to a 5-step build-up on one general line (True Length -> distances -> inclinations theta/phi -> orthographic projections -> traces), all pinning LineCase.INCL_BOTH, with dedicated per-step controls (not cumulative). Teaches the process of constructing views; problem targets dropped case and pin explicit theta/phi. Viewport labels 'line AB'/'end A' are hard-coded.
nodes.norm_label: adr-017: the lines sim is a 5-step problem-solving stepper, not six fixed-orientation cases

nodes.label: ADR-018: Favor textbook fidelity over fudging; reconcile units by a declared scale (1 unit = 10 mm)
nodes.rationale: When a textbook problem does not fit existing controls, add a geometrically-correct control + a per-problem hint rather than fudge a number or drop it. Textbook wording is verbatim; units reconciled by a declared scale 1 world unit = 10 mm, a per-sim label change (Points/Lines show mm, pointData.js stays cm) not a world rescale (toW(v)=v/10 unchanged).
nodes.norm_label: adr-018: favor textbook fidelity over fudging; reconcile units by a declared scale (1 unit = 10 mm)

nodes.label: ADR-019: Verify sims headlessly via Node's built-in WebSocket CDP; no puppeteer, no npm
nodes.rationale: End-to-end verification drives headless Chrome over the DevTools Protocol using Node's built-in WebSocket/fetch (swiftshader software WebGL, cache disabled), never puppeteer/playwright/npm. The final green check must run the shipped module, not a hand-typed replica (a replica once passed while the real module had a call-site bug).
nodes.norm_label: adr-019: verify sims headlessly via node's built-in websocket cdp; no puppeteer, no npm

nodes.label: ADR-020: 'Simple Positions' carries no topic number, and the folder names hide the master
nodes.rationale: Two naming choices: the Simple Positions clone's human-facing title carries no topic number (user preference), and deploy copies are named graphics_module_2_topic_* which do not reveal they are copies of the master. A newcomer cannot infer the master->deploy relationship from the directory listing (known issue).
nodes.norm_label: adr-020: 'simple positions' carries no topic number, and the folder names hide the master

nodes.label: ADR-021: The Lines expanded Compare enters a workbench, true 50/50 with docked live parameters
nodes.rationale: On the Lines side-by-side Compare, collapse the step wizard and re-parent the driver controls (TL, distance HP/VP, theta, phi) into a docked #workbench-rail spanning both panes, gated by cfg.workbenchControls. The reserved wizard otherwise cramped each pane to ~420-490px instead of a true 50/50 and gated live controls away. Re-parents existing .ctrl nodes (one source of truth), never mirrors; rail is hairline-only (Flat-Ink).
nodes.norm_label: adr-021: the lines expanded compare enters a workbench, true 50/50 with docked live parameters

nodes.label: ADR-022: The platform design system is centralized into one root DESIGN.md; per-module DESIGN.shared.md deleted
nodes.rationale: Enacts ADR-010's waited-for end state: the four former design files merged into a single root DESIGN.md audited against live code (code wins), and the three DESIGN.shared.md copies deleted. Removes the drift surface (the copies had drifted ~2 lines); the merge also corrected stale doc claims (scale(0.97) press, 500ms/easeStandard dolly, solid-fill token). Supersedes ADR-010.
nodes.norm_label: adr-022: the platform design system is centralized into one root design.md; per-module design.shared.md deleted

nodes.label: ADR-023: PRODUCT.md is centralized into one root file; per-module copies deleted
nodes.rationale: The two byte-identical per-module product contracts were audited and consolidated into a single root PRODUCT.md; both modules' CLAUDE.md now reference ../PRODUCT.md. Parallels ADR-022; removes the drift surface. The audit flagged two real gaps (Shift+arrow finer steps unimplemented; Module 1 mobile-notice wording diverges).
nodes.norm_label: adr-023: product.md is centralized into one root file; per-module copies deleted

nodes.label: ADR-024: Topic-deploy folders are named graphics_module_<M>_topic_<K>_<slug> for the host catalog
nodes.rationale: Every deployed topic folder encodes subject-module index <M>, host-catalog order <K>, and a lowercase underscore <slug> so the host and a human can read catalog grouping/order from the name. Documents the rationale ADR-020 left descriptive; the numbers serve the catalog, not the master->deploy lineage (still the ADR-020 known issue).
nodes.norm_label: adr-024: topic-deploy folders are named graphics_module_<m>_topic_<k>_<slug> for the host catalog

nodes.label: ADR-025: A new subject module picks its template by geometry; Module 2 for 3D, Module 1 for 2D
nodes.rationale: For a whole new subject: if it manipulates 3D geometry copy Module2/ (the master, with orchestrator, rebuild pipeline, fat lines, mesh analyzer); if it is a sequence of 2D-canvas/diagram lessons copy Module1/. A subject fitting neither cleanly needs its own explicit architectural ADR before work starts; either template still consumes the root DESIGN.md/PRODUCT.md.
nodes.norm_label: adr-025: a new subject module picks its template by geometry; module 2 for 3d, module 1 for 2d

nodes.label: ADR-026: A sim's <title> in index.html must match the title field in meta.json
nodes.rationale: index.html <title> must equal meta.json.title: one human-facing name in two places. meta.json.title is the host catalog entry; <title> is the browser tab and the screen-reader accessible name, so a mismatch is both a catalog and accessibility defect. Topic 2 shipped a mismatch, fixed 2026-06-28. (Module 1 is seven pages under one meta.json, so per-lesson titles are by design.)
nodes.norm_label: adr-026: a sim's <title> in index.html must match the title field in meta.json

nodes.label: ADR-027: iShape.js is an adapt file, not a copy-identical shared file
nodes.rationale: iShape.js is adapt-on-copy, NOT one of the byte-identical shared files, because it carries topic-specific pose logic (the restingPlane VP lay-down quaternion, angleHP/angleVP inclination signs, explicit ZXY Euler). The master (4702 bytes) and topics (Topic 2 is 2652 bytes) legitimately diverge; copying it verbatim is a documented trap. The pure geometry generators next to it stay identical.
nodes.norm_label: adr-027: ishape.js is an adapt file, not a copy-identical shared file

nodes.label: ADR-028: A new topic consumes the root DESIGN.md/PRODUCT.md, never a local copy
nodes.rationale: A new topic must reference the root ../DESIGN.md and ../PRODUCT.md via its CLAUDE.md and never create local copies. Makes ADR-022/ADR-023's centralization durable: every per-file copy is a drift point (the two DESIGN.shared.md copies had already drifted). A convenience local stub is just a copy that will drift.
nodes.norm_label: adr-028: a new topic consumes the root design.md/product.md, never a local copy

nodes.label: ADR-029: Foundations adopts the orchestrator pattern + a per-edge line-of-sight hidden-line classifier
nodes.rationale: Foundations is rebuilt on Module 2's orchestrator pattern (superseding ADR-011 for this topic only), teaching BIS line types on an orbitable 3D Bearing Block. Retains meshAnalyzer.js and adds a net-new per-edge raycast occlusion classifier (lineDrawer.js) re-run on orbit (rAF-throttled). Module 2's convex normal.y>0 shortcut fails on the non-convex part; a Phase-3 depth-buffer attempt was reverted because it cannot draw dashed hidden lines.
nodes.norm_label: adr-029: foundations adopts the orchestrator pattern + a per-edge line-of-sight hidden-line classifier

nodes.label: ADR-030: Accelerate occlusion raycasting with three-mesh-bvh via the CDN import map
nodes.rationale: Add three-mesh-bvh (pinned, jsDelivr) to the same import map as three@0.160.0 to accelerate ADR-029's per-edge occlusion raycasts. A BVH turns each ray from O(triangles) to ~O(log triangles), the precondition for dropping the debounce (ADR-031). It ships as an ES module pinnable like three, so no npm/bundler/build (stays inside ADR-001). The BVH is derived state, rebuilt and disposed with the mesh.
nodes.norm_label: adr-030: accelerate occlusion raycasting with three-mesh-bvh via the cdn import map

nodes.label: ADR-031: Replace the occlusion debounce timer with real-time requestAnimationFrame throttling
nodes.rationale: The ~100ms occlusion debounce (recompute after the student stops moving) is removed; the visible/hidden reclassification now runs one pass per requestAnimationFrame, dirty-gated on real camera movement. The debounce only masked naive-raycasting cost; with the BVH (ADR-030) per-frame is affordable so edges flip visible<->hidden live. Establishes: heavy continuous-input updates are rAF-throttled + dirty-gated, never debounced.
nodes.norm_label: adr-031: replace the occlusion debounce timer with real-time requestanimationframe throttling

nodes.label: ADR-032: The floating padded scrollbar pill is the platform scrollbar standard, tinted --color-border
nodes.rationale: Scroll containers show a floating padded pill (10px channel, 3px transparent border + background-clip:padding-box so only ~4px paints), tinted --color-border (~1.28:1). scrollbar-width is left UNSET on the base rule (only set inside a Firefox @supports guard) so Chrome 121+ keeps the ::-webkit-scrollbar pseudo-elements. Serves Visibility of System Status while staying quiet (Quiet Chrome); --color-panel was too invisible and --color-bench-grey too loud.
nodes.norm_label: adr-032: the floating padded scrollbar pill is the platform scrollbar standard, tinted --color-border

nodes.label: ADR-033: Module 1 fully adopts the orchestrator pattern, fully superseding ADR-011
nodes.rationale: Module 1's four remaining topics (Quadrants, First-angle, Points, Lines) migrate off shared engine.js onto Module 2's orchestrator + leaf-module pattern, each a standalone graphics_module_1_topic_* folder cut from the Module 2 skeleton. Quadrants+First-angle ship combined as 'Spatial Framework'. A platform-wide commitment, not a per-topic exception; fully supersedes ADR-011 and removes the two-architecture cognitive tax. engine.js is retired as a template.
nodes.norm_label: adr-033: module 1 fully adopts the orchestrator pattern, fully superseding adr-011

nodes.label: ADR-034: The migrated Points Compare card draws its 2D sheet on one 2D <canvas>, not a second WebGL stack
nodes.rationale: graphics_module_1_topic_3_points honours ADR-012 but renders the Compare card's 2D orthographic drawing on a plain 2D <canvas> owned by the card's stage, repainted per rebuild, instead of re-housing the legacy second WebGL scene (S2/#c2d). A point's sheet is five primitives; a second WebGLRenderer would double GL contexts (context exhaustion is the most likely late-stage bug). Phase-6: now renders the PP lateral coordinate instead of centring it.
nodes.norm_label: adr-034: the migrated points compare card draws its 2d sheet on one 2d <canvas>, not a second webgl stack

nodes.label: ADR-036: Restore the 3D-to-2D orthographic camera swoop during the fold
nodes.rationale: Overturns ADR-013's held-angle revision: the fold-to-flat again flies the front-on orthographic camera swoop with a perspective->ortho morph, landing square-on on the finished 2D sheet as the textbook prints it; the held-angle dolly (animateFoldHold) is retired. The held fold ended on a foreshortened sheet; landing square-on closes the 3D->2D loop in one move. Landed 2026-07-10 (animateFoldSwoop / swoopToAnswerSheet). The first reversal (camera does move) still binds.
nodes.norm_label: adr-036: restore the 3d-to-2d orthographic camera swoop during the fold

nodes.label: ADR-037: The standalone Points Compare gains a true 50/50 workbench, in its own architecture
nodes.rationale: Brings Points Compare to parity with the Lines workbench (ADR-021): expanding Compare enters a true 50/50 split (wizard collapses, 3D left, 2D right, four point drivers docked in #workbench-rail). Built entirely in the topic's own code (DOM re-parent + body.compare-split grid + stepper.refresh), NOT via initSim cfg keys, which do not exist post-ADR-033. Re-parents existing [data-ctrl] wrappers; the 2D-canvas right pane keeps the single-canvas invariant. Strikes ADR-021's 'Points omits workbench' clause.
nodes.norm_label: adr-037: the standalone points compare gains a true 50/50 workbench, in its own architecture

nodes.label: ADR-038: The 2D Compare orthographic drawing is a FIXED scale locked to the static sheet bounds
nodes.rationale: The on-demand Compare 2D orthographic drawing renders at a fixed scale locked to the static SHEET bounds (Lines: SHEET2D_SPAN=(SHEET/2)*10), so a real millimetre always reads the same on-screen length; it must not auto-fit. The orthographic sheet is a measured drawing; auto-zoom would shrink 10 mm as True Length grows and break the side-by-side comparison. ADR-014's clip-aware auto-zoom applies only to the 3D perspective main pane.
nodes.norm_label: adr-038: the 2d compare orthographic drawing is a fixed scale locked to the static sheet bounds

nodes.label: Creative North Star: The Patient Tutor's Paper
nodes.rationale: The surface a patient one-on-one tutor works on: a clean clinical sheet (pure-white #ffffff base, neutral-gray #f5f5f5 working surfaces, dark ink) matching the host-site palette so the sim reads as one seamless page. Patience lives in the voice, pacing and quiet chrome, not tint; saturated colour is rationed to two jobs only - the functional engineering encodings and the one blue accent. Rewritten 2026-07-09, retiring the former warm off-white drafting-paper framing.
nodes.norm_label: creative north star: the patient tutor's paper

nodes.label: Clinical / Inverted Palette and token table
nodes.rationale: The live CSS custom-property colour system (paper #ffffff, panel #f5f5f5, solid-fill #e7e1d4, ink #221f18, accent #1f66b5, hp-line teal #007f7c, vp-line amber #bc5d1e, pp-line violet #7a5ea6, success #2e7d52, plus Module-1 construction-aid tokens). Authored in OKLCH for intent, stored as resolved sRGB hex because THREE.Color cannot parse oklch(). Paper/panel tones were swapped and content surfaces returned to white in the 2026-07-09 clinical-palette phase.
nodes.norm_label: clinical / inverted palette and token table

nodes.label: The Quiet Chrome Rule
nodes.rationale: The blue accent covers at most ~10% of any screen; if more than a tenth of the chrome is blue it is overused. The eye must land on the viewport, not the UI.

nodes.label: The Chrome-Only Blue Rule
nodes.rationale: Blue belongs to the guidance layer (steps, actions, focus) and never appears as a domain colour inside the viewport, which uses the functional encodings (HP teal, VP amber). This separation lets a learner tell 'the UI is guiding me' from 'this is the domain content' even on a washed-out projector.

nodes.label: The Two-Cue Rule
nodes.rationale: No colour carries meaning alone; every functional encoding pairs its hue with a second cue - line weight, dash pattern, label, icon, arrow, or shape. HP is teal + solid + 'HP' label; VP amber + dashed + 'VP'; PP violet + label + position; Success green + check; Disabled faint + reduced opacity + lock icon. CVD-safe.

nodes.label: The Two-Weight Rule
nodes.rationale: Atkinson Hyperlegible ships Regular (400) and Bold (700) only. Build hierarchy from size and the 700 bold, never from a 500/600 weight that does not exist (and never synthesize bold).

nodes.label: The Tabular Rule
nodes.rationale: Every value the math depends on is set in IBM Plex Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so it does not shift width as it updates. Showing real values in real units is the line between an engineering instrument and a toy.

nodes.label: The Flat-Ink Rule
nodes.rationale: Surfaces are flat at rest; depth is tonal layering (paper -> panel -> solid-fill) and 1px hairlines, not shadows. Rendered geometry never casts a shadow; a shadow is only legitimate lifting a transient floating overlay off the page.

nodes.label: The Border-Over-Shadow Rule
nodes.rationale: Structure comes from a single crisp 1px hairline (#d9d2c3) and tonal layering, not a drop shadow. Cards and panels are separated by tone and seam, not by float.

nodes.label: The Host-Integration White Exception (retired 2026-07-09)
nodes.rationale: Under the clinical palette the separate --color-host-white token is gone from the code. Former consumers split by role: content surfaces (step card, #active-problem, .problem-card, .problem-library, .compare-card frame) sit on paper #ffffff, while chrome chips (wizard toggle, quick-views, .vp-hint/spotlights) sit on the neutral-gray panel #f5f5f5 shell. Token discipline unchanged: never a bare #fff/#000 literal.

nodes.label: The z-index ladder
nodes.rationale: A single ordered ladder of tokens so transient layers never fight: --z-term 60, --z-compare 90, --z-notice 100, --z-overlay 120, --z-toast 130, --z-restoring 150, --z-boot 200 (full ladder in Module1/src/shell.css). Never hard-code a z-index. Module 2 defines only the two rungs it needs (--z-notice, --z-overlay).

nodes.label: The no-transform invariant (Module 1)
nodes.rationale: #sim-viewport, #canvas-area and body must stay transform-free. Module 1's Compare card floats its #c2d canvas position:fixed from measured viewport rects; a CSS transform on any ancestor would establish a containing block and break that placement.

nodes.label: Wizard layout - the right-hand column
nodes.rationale: The guided stepper is a fixed-width vertical column pinned right (width clamp(340px,34vw,460px)) beside the flexible left 3D viewport, separated by a 1px border-left. Strict background mandate: viewport is --color-paper #ffffff, wizard panel is --color-panel #f5f5f5, never swapped. Module 1 additionally carries the .brand wordmark and .chapnav switcher (Module-1-specific).

nodes.label: Step rail (signature component)
nodes.rationale: A vertical numbered spine: Completed = Success-green disc + check glyph, Current = filled accent disc + soft halo + bold label, Upcoming = hollow faint disc. Shape + number carries state without relying on colour; a live region announces 'Step X of N'. Learners may revisit any step up to maxReached.

nodes.label: Inline term definition (signature component)
nodes.rationale: First appearance of engineering vocabulary (HP, VP, orthographic projection, ground line) is a dotted-underline accent button that reveals a small accent-wash popover (#e3ecf7) defining the term in plain language; exposed to screen readers via aria-describedby. position:fixed to escape the card scroll clip, flips above when no room, dismisses on Escape.

nodes.label: Motion palette and press conventions
nodes.rationale: CSS keyframes plus a rAF tween system (anim.js) with a no-overshoot named easing palette (easeStandard, easeFold, easeCamera, easeDraw, easeDissolve); everything collapses to instant under prefers-reduced-motion. Base tokens --dur-fast 150ms, --dur-base 200ms, --dur-step 380ms, --ease-standard cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1). Every pressable control shares the scale(0.97) press; auto-zoom dolly is 500ms/easeStandard.

nodes.label: Scrollbars - the floating padded pill
nodes.rationale: Scroll containers show a floating padded scrollbar pill (10px WebKit channel, 3px transparent border + background-clip:padding-box so ~4px paints), tinted --color-border, border-radius 999px, transparent track. Load-bearing gotcha: leave scrollbar-width UNSET on the base rule (set only inside a Firefox @supports guard) or Chrome 121+ disables the ::-webkit-scrollbar pseudo-elements.

nodes.label: Typography - Atkinson Hyperlegible + IBM Plex Mono
nodes.rationale: Body/UI font is Atkinson Hyperlegible; numeric font is IBM Plex Mono; these are the only fonts, bundled as subset woff2 via @font-face (Atkinson 400/700, Plex Mono 400), no external font CDN. Roles: Title/Lead/Body/Label in Atkinson, every live numeric Value plus the mono 'Step X of N' eyebrow in Plex Mono.
nodes.norm_label: typography - atkinson hyperlegible + ibm plex mono

nodes.label: Master -> deploy map (Module2/ is the master)
nodes.rationale: The single most important thing a newcomer cannot infer from folder names: Module2/ is THE MASTER (Orthographic Projection of Solids), the graphics_module_2_topic_* folders are deployed copies of it, and Module1/ is its own module (not a copy). Originate every change in the master first, then copy/adapt; never fix a shared file directly in a topic; never infer lineage from a topic_N number.
nodes.norm_label: master -> deploy map (module2/ is the master)

nodes.label: Byte-identical shared files vs adapt files
nodes.rationale: Some files must stay byte-identical across the Module-2 family: anim.js, the geometry generators (cube/cone/cylinder/genericPrism/genericPyramid/genericSolid), and meshAnalyzer.js (master + topic clones + Foundations). iShape.js is the exception - an adapt file carrying topic-specific pose logic. There is no automated sync, so any shared-file fix must be re-copied to every carrier or the copies drift.
nodes.norm_label: byte-identical shared files vs adapt files

nodes.label: Points Compare-Split Workbench
nodes.rationale: A true 50/50 Compare-split workbench built in the Points topic's own standalone architecture (DOM re-parenting of driver controls into a docked rail + a body.compare-split CSS grid), NOT via the shared engine's initSim keys, because Points was migrated off engine.js (ADR-033). Single-WebGL-canvas invariant preserved.

nodes.label: 3D-to-2D Orthographic Fold Swoop
nodes.rationale: The fold now SWOOPS square-on to the orthographic answer sheet (ADR-036), overturning ADR-013's held-angle hold; the held-angle movers (animateFoldHold/framePerspectiveToFlat) are deleted and preFoldPose is no longer stored since the perspective camera never moves during the swoop.

nodes.label: Lines 2D Compare Sheet-Locked Scale
nodes.rationale: The 2D Compare drawing is a fixed sheet-locked scale (SHEET2D_SPAN derived from SHEET = (SHEET/2)*10 = 300mm per half), never auto-zooming, so a real mm reads the same on-screen length at any True Length and the worst-case line never overflows the sheet.

nodes.label: System-Wide Ortho Orbit Lock
nodes.rationale: enableRotate=false on every dual-camera ortho OrbitControls pair, with a qv-lock-cue shake+ring nudge on the latched quick-view chip when a left-drag is attempted in a locked ortho view.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar Harmonization
nodes.rationale: ADR-032 system-wide scrollbar harmonization: WebKit thumb + Firefox scrollbar-color retinted to --color-border everywhere, replacing accent-blue tints and hidden scrollbars, so learners get a 'more content below' cue in the Quiet-Chrome style (hiding a scrollbar fails Visibility of System Status).

nodes.label: Clinical Palette Reversal
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 palette inverted paper/panel tones (--color-paper #ffffff, --color-panel #f5f5f5) across all 7 shells so the viewport is white and panels are gray; retires the warm-paper 'deliberately not clinical' framing for the web team's clinical palette. WCAG contrast re-measurement flagged mandatory.

nodes.label: Quadrant Numeral Occlusion
nodes.rationale: Quadrant numerals I-IV now occlude behind the HP/VP sheets via a per-frame updateOcclusion() raycast from the live camera, since CSS2D labels bypass the depth buffer; also moved to far outer corners so they never overlap point P or projectors.

nodes.label: Spatial Framework Topic
nodes.rationale: Quadrants + First-angle combined into one Module-1 topic built on the Module 2 orchestrator pattern (ADR-033): a 5-step 'Room & Shadow' guided stepper reusing the platform's cinematic fold animation, with Point P distances clamped 1-40cm to enforce quadrant pedagogy.

nodes.label: Foundations Topic (Bearing Block)
nodes.rationale: An orbitable 3D bearing block teaching the four BIS line types with a live line-of-sight (raycast) hidden-line classifier, built on the Module 2 orchestrator pattern and retaining meshAnalyzer.js (ADR-029 supersedes ADR-011 for this topic only).

nodes.label: three-mesh-bvh Occlusion Acceleration
nodes.rationale: Integrated three-mesh-bvh through the CDN import map to accelerate the non-convex occlusion raycaster (ADR-030), and replaced the ~100ms debounce with rAF throttling dirty-gated on camera movement (ADR-031) so hidden lines update live as the part orbits, preserving the no-build contract.

nodes.label: PLATFORM-RULES.md Extraction
nodes.rationale: Extracted the subject-agnostic subset of RULES.md (platform contract, UI & Visual, generic Cross-Subject Harmony, Documentation) so a new engineering-discipline module has a ready checklist without Engineering-Graphics-specific rules.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.module-template.md
nodes.rationale: A starter CLAUDE.md for a brand-new Simatrix subject module carrying only the platform-wide contract, with an explicit instruction that a new subject must author its own ARCHITECTURE/DECISIONS/RULES docs before writing simulation code.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Centralization
nodes.rationale: One consolidated code-audited platform design system merged from four former per-module DESIGN.md / DESIGN.shared.md copies (ADR-022 supersedes ADR-010), so the visual contract has a single source of truth instead of four drifting copies.

nodes.label: PRODUCT.md Centralization
nodes.rationale: One consolidated code-audited platform product contract merged from two former byte-identical per-module PRODUCT.md files (ADR-023, parallels ADR-022) so persona/anti-references/principles/accessibility commitments have a single source of truth.

nodes.label: Root Enforcement Docs (RULES/DECISIONS/ARCHITECTURE)
nodes.rationale: RULES.md (120 DO/NEVER enforcement rules), DECISIONS.md (ADR log recording WHY key choices were made), and ARCHITECTURE.md (whole-repo architecture map) established so every documented decision is actionable and future contributors don't accidentally undo reversed decisions.

nodes.label: MODULE-STARTER.md Playbook
nodes.rationale: A from-scratch code-verified playbook for creating a new sim (new Module 2 topic, new Module 1 lesson, or new subject module), with byte-identical file lists confirmed by md5sum and a pre-ship verification checklist citing its RULES/ADR/DESIGN sources.

nodes.label: Simatrix Platform
nodes.rationale: A platform of interactive simulations helping B.Tech students build intuition for engineering concepts across disciplines; each sim ships as a sandboxed iframe payload teaching as a Guided Stepper. Success = a struggling first-year understands the first step in 30 seconds and can verify a textbook problem.

nodes.label: Guided Stepper
nodes.rationale: A progressive-disclosure wizard that sequences one concept at a time, moving the learner through Orient then Intuition then Problem-solving; replaces the overwhelming all-controls-at-once dashboard.

nodes.label: Brand Personality (Patient, Encouraging, Clear)
nodes.rationale: A warm one-on-one tutor sitting beside the student; encouragement delivered only through tone and a quiet sense of progress, never through game mechanics (no points/streaks/badges/confetti/mascots). Reference lane: GeoGebra, Desmos, Wokwi, Falstad, Tinkercad.

nodes.label: Anti-References (Product Boundaries)
nodes.rationale: Five locked-out boundaries: Gamified EdTech, Glossy/architectural-viz aesthetic, Marketing-site polish, Hard industry-tool mimicry, and the Overwhelming dashboard; they set the boundary for visual, interaction, and copy decisions on every screen.

nodes.label: Seven Core Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Seven strategic principles that override taste in conflicts and apply uniformly across all disciplines: struggling-learner-first, one-idea-per-step, one-language-many-disciplines, show-real-values, educational-scaffolding-industry-vocabulary, inclusive-by-default, and quiet-chrome-loud-subject.

nodes.label: Design for the Struggling Learner First
nodes.rationale: The tie-breaker meta-principle: when a decision helps the confident student but risks losing the anxious first-year, the weaker learner wins. Deliberately NOT a RULES.md checklist item because it cannot be mechanically verified.
nodes.norm_label: design for the struggling learner first

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome, Loud Subject
nodes.rationale: Every UI pixel that is not the simulation viewport stays quiet enough that the math/geometry is what the eye lands on; restrained color (~10% blue accent), minimal decoration, no surface that competes with sim content.

nodes.label: Module 1 — Foundations of Projection
nodes.rationale: Seven live 3D guided-stepper lessons on one shared engine: five intro lessons (reference planes, types of lines, dimensioning, four quadrants, first-angle projection) plus two simulations (Projection of Points, Projection of Straight Lines).

nodes.label: Module 2 — Orthographic Projection of Solids
nodes.rationale: The master codebase: six gated steps flattening a hard-edged solid (cube, prism, pyramid, cylinder, cone) to a 2D orthographic drawing, with a parameter dock, rotation priority hierarchy, and vertex labeling; every change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline.

nodes.label: Compare View
nodes.rationale: The main pane is always the live 3D scene; the 2D textbook drawing (or a live-rebuilt 3D view while folded) appears on demand in a floating Compare card, with a docked side-by-side split for Points/Lines.

nodes.label: Cinematic Reversible Fold/Unfold
nodes.rationale: The HP plane hinges flat onto the VP about the xy fold line and back again, either holding the learner's own 3D viewing angle (Points/Lines) or sweeping square-on (First-angle).

nodes.label: Lines Workbench
nodes.rationale: The expanded Compare split collapses the wizard for a true 50/50 and docks the live driver controls (True Length, distance HP/VP, theta, phi) under both panes (ADR-021) — the one deliberate exception to progressive disclosure, for the solve-and-verify phase.

nodes.label: Problem Library
nodes.rationale: Tiered textbook problems with hints revealed one at a time and a ±0.5-tolerant self-check that never auto-fills; the student dials the setup and the check lights green, making the sim a verification tool not a toy.

nodes.label: Inline Term Glossary
nodes.rationale: Dotted-underline terms open a tooltip on hover/focus/click fed by per-lesson TERMS data, providing an inline definition the first time a textbook term appears without replacing the term itself.

nodes.label: Dual Perspective/Orthographic Camera
nodes.rationale: Top/Front/Side orthographic quick-view chips with a perspective-to-ortho morph, plus clip-aware auto-zoom and a connector/projector declutter toggle.

nodes.label: Parameter Dock
nodes.rationale: Module 2's uiManager controls: base length, height, distance HP/VP, angle HP/VP, manual Y rotation; every slider paired two-way with a clamped numeric input tolerating a decimal comma.

nodes.label: Accessibility Commitments (WCAG 2.2 AA)
nodes.rationale: WCAG 2.2 AA target: color never the only signal (two-cue rule), contrast, full keyboard access with visible focus, reduced-motion honored, screen-reader announcements, and legibility-first Atkinson Hyperlegible typography. Accessibility is a defining goal, not a compliance afterthought.

nodes.label: Primary Persona — Struggling First-Year
nodes.rationale: The person every decision is optimized for: a first-year who finds orthographic projection abstract and intimidating, with no CAD/MATLAB exposure, who quietly assumes they are 'bad at this'. Used across self-study, classroom, and assessment contexts.

nodes.label: Points/Lines Fold Swoop (Module 1)
nodes.rationale: The shared engine's held-angle dolly replaced by animateFoldSwoop/snapFoldSwoop on the dual-camera stack: forward engages the ortho camera and glides it front-on to the flattened sheet morphing perspective to ortho on the easeFold curve; drives both Module 1 sims (Points via main.js, Lines via lines.js).

nodes.label: Lines Side-by-Side Compare Split
nodes.rationale: Opening Lines Compare collapses the step panel and docks the True Length/distance/angle sliders in a slim strip beneath the two drawings (live 3D left, 2D orthographic right) for a true 50/50 split, replacing the floating PiP card that hovered over the 3D view.

nodes.label: HT/VT Trace Markers
nodes.rationale: HT/VT trace markers now appear in the live 3D scene during the 'Show Traces' walkthrough — a teal dot where the line pierces HP, an amber dot where it pierces VP, each with a dashed extension — so traces read in 3D, not only in the 2D construction (off-sheet traces suppressed).

nodes.label: Lines 5-Step Problem-Solving Stepper
nodes.rationale: The Lines sim reworked into a 5-step stepper (True Length, Distance from HP/VP, Inclinations, Generate Orthographic Projections, Draw Traces) built on one general line the learner sets up, each step exposing only its own control, replacing six fixed-orientation exploration steps.

nodes.label: N.D. Bhatt / K.C. John Textbook Problem Sets
nodes.rationale: Authentic N.D. Bhatt / K.C. John textbook problem sets for the Points and Lines Problem Libraries (points across the four quadrants plus on-plane cases; lines from parallel-to-both through inclined-to-both), with flexible 'OR' answer acceptance for geometrically degenerate quadrants.
nodes.norm_label: n.d. bhatt / k.c. john textbook problem sets

nodes.label: Dual-Camera Orchestrator Port
nodes.rationale: Ported Module 2's full camera/animation orchestrator into the shared engine — dual perspective/orthographic cameras with active-camera switching, a projection-matrix morph (projectionMorphK) for seamless 3D<->2D transitions, clip-aware auto-zoom, orthographic quick-views, and a flattened 2D pan — gated to the Points/Lines sims.

nodes.label: Points/Lines Auto-Zoom Framing
nodes.rationale: Engine hardening: the auto-zoom frames the subject on the geometry's centre so the camera pulls back linearly as a parameter grows (killing the off-centre 'exponential lurch'), and the view opens snug on the default geometry, easing back only as values grow, via Module 2's one-shot fixed-duration eased dolly.

nodes.label: Step-Card Scrollbar Pill (Module 1)
nodes.rationale: shell.css .step-card's fully-hidden scrollbar replaced with the platform floating padded pill (ADR-032): 10px WebKit channel, transparent track, --color-border thumb floating clear via a 3px transparent padding-box border, with a Firefox @supports guard. Hiding a scrollbar fails Visibility of System Status.

nodes.label: Floating Minimal Scrollbars (Module 2)
nodes.rationale: Backported the floating minimal scrollbars (ADR-032) to #step-card and .problem-library__body — the hidden scrollbar replaced by a 10px WebKit channel with a ~4px --color-border pill floating clear via a 3px transparent padding-box border, so learners get a 'more content below' cue in the Quiet-Chrome style.

nodes.label: White Card/Chip Surfaces
nodes.rationale: White card/chip surfaces (--color-host-white) so the sim blends with the white host page when embedded.

nodes.label: Design Tokens (:root)
nodes.rationale: The single source of truth for every colour, space, and motion value, read by JS via getComputedStyle. Neutrals authored in OKLCH and stored as resolved sRGB hex (since THREE.Color cannot parse oklch); no #000/#fff anywhere. Clinical palette: paper #ffffff, panel #f5f5f5.

nodes.label: Guided Stepper Chrome (Rail + Card)
nodes.rationale: A vertical numbered step rail (progress spine, is-complete/is-current/is-upcoming) beside the step card (the tutor panel); upcoming steps render disabled and out of tab order so the rail is a map you can only walk back along, never skip ahead.

nodes.label: Sim Viewport (WebGL + CSS2D)
nodes.rationale: The WebGL canvas plus the CSS2D label overlay (vertex labels, plane labels, reference-line labels, view-name captions), positioned on the left with the wizard on the right; drag-to-orbit disables text selection and touch scrolling.

nodes.label: Quick-View Camera Chips
nodes.rationale: A segmented pill group (Top/Front/Side) in the top-left .vp-cluster; the latched view fills solid accent, and clicking it again returns to perspective orbit.

nodes.label: Connector-Line Toggle
nodes.rationale: A pill toggle beneath the quick-view group that fills solid accent when on (declutter of connector/projector lines); the hidden checkbox makes the chip itself the on/off affordance, reflected via :has().

nodes.label: Orbit-Lock Cue (qv-lock-cue)
nodes.rationale: A drag on a rotate-locked ortho view nudges the latched chip with a shake+ring animation ('disengage this view to orbit'); reduced motion keeps the ring but drops the shake.

nodes.label: Boot Watchdog / Sim Fallback
nodes.rationale: A classic-script watchdog arming a self-healing fallback if the pinned Three.js CDN module (the sim's only runtime network dependency) fails to load or WebGL is unavailable; main.js clears it on successful boot so a merely-slow load self-heals. The struggling learner reads a calm explanation, not a void.

nodes.label: Three.js CDN Import Map
nodes.rationale: Three.js loaded as CDN ES modules only, pinned to 0.160.0, with no build step/bundler/npm — the exact import-map contract required by the platform.

nodes.label: Mobile Notice
nodes.rationale: A dismissible 'Best experienced on desktop' banner at <768px (#mobile-notice, role=status) that never blocks the sim — the platform contract advisory.

nodes.label: Success Toast
nodes.rationale: A calm win confirmation for 'Complete & next problem' — success green plus a check glyph (two-cue rule), a transient floating surface that earns the overlay shadow (Flat-Ink exception), never gamified fanfare.

nodes.label: Two-State Reset Confirm
nodes.rationale: The ghost Reset arms into a quiet 'Reset everything? · Yes / Cancel' on the same spot so a stray click can't wipe the drawing; only 'Yes' calls simAPI.reset() (single reset path).

nodes.label: Slider + Numeric Field Control
nodes.rationale: A borderless 14px accent dot thumb on a thin 3px pill track with a 44px transparent hit-area; paired with a right-aligned tabular-nums numeric field, following the thin-visual / full-hit pattern.

nodes.label: First-Angle Projection Symbol
nodes.rationale: A screen-space HTML/SVG annotation pinned bottom-right, hidden until the drawing flattens (Step 5) then faded in; a pure overlay (not a scene object) so it stays put during orbit.

nodes.label: Domain Colours (HP/VP/PP Encoding)
nodes.rationale: Viewport-only projection encodings: HP teal SOLID (#007f7c), VP amber DASHED (#bc5d1e), PP violet (#7a5ea6) — a CVD-safe pair held off the chrome blue, each carrying a non-colour cue (Two-Cue Rule) and meeting AA on paper.

nodes.label: Onboarding Hints (Orbit + Spotlight)
nodes.rationale: A one-time dismissible orbit-discovery chip (auto-dismissed on first drag) plus contextual spotlight hints with a leading colour dot tying the hint to its linework (teal HP / amber VP / ink connectors), played one at a time so they never stack.

nodes.label: Wizard Hide/Show Toggle
nodes.rationale: A floating 44px control pinned to the viewport's top-right that collapses the step panel for a larger 3D view (body.wizard-collapsed) and brings it back; the chevron flips when collapsed and the viewport reflows to full width via flex.

nodes.label: Bearing Block Model
nodes.rationale: The orbitable 3D split plummer/pillow block is the lesson subject because it yields all four BIS line types in one view and makes visible edges become hidden edges as it spins; the body no longer redraws the full base slab to avoid non-manifold 'spiderweb' edges and false occlusion.

nodes.label: Hidden-Line Occlusion Raycaster
nodes.rationale: The CPU line-of-sight occlusion raycaster (accelerated by three-mesh-bvh) is REQUIRED, not an optimisation: it makes the visible-Type-A vs hidden-Type-E/F decision that produces dashed lines, the topic's whole reason to exist. Phase 3 tried to drop it for a GPU depth-buffer X-ray and broke the lesson; it was reverted (ADR-029 addendum / ADR-030). Runs live per rAF on orbit.

nodes.label: Front View Projection Morph
nodes.rationale: A dual-camera projectionMorphK matrix blend eases perspective to orthographic so the Front View lands on a true parallel elevation with no 'pop'; dragging or scrolling out eases smoothly back to free-orbit 3D via a single guarded morph so a continued gesture can't fight it.

nodes.label: Line Classification Fixes
nodes.rationale: Math/classification-layer fixes in lineDrawer.js: a coplanar-coverage flush-seam filter drops the false body/foot seam, edge subdivision into ~0.5-unit sub-segments lets a long arris draw solid then dashed exactly where it leaves view, and negating buried contact-face normals stops genuine creases self-occluding while orbiting.

nodes.label: BIS Line-Type Stepper
nodes.rationale: Four-step guided reveal (Type A / Type E-F / Type G / Type B) driven by foundationSteps.js; adds strict BIS 3:1 solid-filled arrowheads, an Aligned vs Unidirectional dimension-text toggle, and an 'Inspect arrowhead' micro-zoom, so completion latches the moment Type B dimensions are revealed.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Foundations)
nodes.rationale: The step-card scroll region shows a floating padded pill tinted to --color-border (ADR-032 Quiet Chrome) instead of a hidden scrollbar, giving a 'more content below' cue; scrollbar-width stays unset on the base rule so Chrome 121+ keeps the WebKit pseudo-elements.

nodes.label: Orbitable Bearing Block Viewport
nodes.rationale: #sim-viewport hosts the WebGL canvas plus a CSS2D overlay of BIS line-type callouts and dimension-value pills; live OrbitControls let the learner spin the part and watch line classification change.

nodes.label: BIS Line-Type Wizard
nodes.rationale: The right-dock guided wizard: a 4-item vertical step rail (Type A / E-F / G / B) beside a white step card with Reveal hidden lines / Reveal centre lines / Reveal dimensions buttons and a pinned Back/Next/Reset footer.

nodes.label: Dimension Text Toggle
nodes.rationale: A Step-4 segmented control (Aligned vs Unidirectional) that rotates the vertical height dimension value, letting learners compare the two BIS dimensioning systems live.

nodes.label: Glossary Term Popover
nodes.rationale: One shared fixed #term-pop, filled by terms.js, defines inline dotted-underline .term words on hover/focus/tap; delegated so re-injected step bodies need no re-wiring.

nodes.label: Turn 90 Viewport Chip
nodes.rationale: A floating viewport pill that rotates the part in 90-degree steps so a keyboard-only learner can watch visible edges become hidden without a mouse drag.

nodes.label: Rabattement Fold (Flatten-to-2D)
nodes.rationale: The step-4 fold is a dual-camera event: swoopToAnswerSheet flies an OrthographicCamera square-on while projectionMorphK blends perspective to orthographic over the 1600 ms easeFold hinge, so the folded corner reads as a true flat first-angle drawing; restorePerspective glides back to the 3D orbit.

nodes.label: Orbital Quadrant Flights
nodes.rationale: flyCamera sweeps a TRUE spherical orbit (quaternion slerp of the offset direction + radius/pivot lerp) and each Q1-Q4 pose sits physically inside its own room, so an east-west walk genuinely crosses behind the VP wall instead of cutting a straight chord through the corner.

nodes.label: HP/VP Plane Pair
nodes.rationale: hvPlanes.js draws the teal HP / amber VP pair with faint fills and a dense 'cage' grid; the beyond-fold extension is always built and faded independently via setExtendedOpacity so the shared Quadrant-I corner never re-fades or double-draws, and the HP sits in a pivot hinged on the X fold line. VP sheet border is solid amber by explicit override of the Two-Cue dash pairing.

nodes.label: Point Projector Rig
nodes.rationale: point.js draws P (ink sphere + paper halo) and its thick-dot top/front views p and p', with dashed fat-line projectors starting SPHERE_GAP off P so the dash begins cleanly at the sphere surface (Linux GL dash-shader fix); the on-VP p'-to-fold-line connector stays solid while the 3D VP projector stays dashed.

nodes.label: Frustum Illustration
nodes.rationale: frustums.js draws the step-5 classic textbook figure: cone frustums in Quadrants I and III (Q3 the point-reflection) with concentric-circle top views on HP and trapezoid front views on VP; the Q3 body carries renderOrder -3 so it draws beneath the translucent sheet grids for the 'cage' read and the transparent-to-opaque flip stays seamless.

nodes.label: Spatial Quadrant Label Layer
nodes.rationale: labelLayer.js owns the CSS2D HP/VP/XY callouts, boxed P/p/p' chips and I-IV quadrant numerals; a per-frame updateOcclusion raycasts camera to numeral against the sheet FILL meshes (Line2 grids excluded) and hides occluded numerals, running after renderer.render and before the CSS2D re-projection.

nodes.label: Transition Cross-Fades
nodes.rationale: A per-leaf fadeState opacity multiplier (re-stamped after every rebuild so a mid-fade rebuild never snaps) plus an always-disposed fade-out graveyard let applyView fade planes up on grow and cross-fade the point rig against the frustums across the 4-5 boundary; steps 1-3 carry foldPose:'unfolded' so back-nav auto-reverses the fold.

nodes.label: Room & Shadow Stepper
nodes.rationale: A Module-2-pattern guided-step controller (stepper.js) rendering the 5-step 'Room & Shadow' sequence (Reference Planes to Standard) from pure-data spatialSteps.js, gating Next behind the step-4 fold and pushing each step's view flags to the orchestrator via applyView.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Spatial)
nodes.rationale: The #step-card scrollbar pill was retinted from --color-accent to --color-border per ADR-032 Quiet Chrome (WebKit thumb + Firefox scrollbar-color).

nodes.label: HP/VP Viewport
nodes.rationale: #sim-viewport mounts the WebGL canvas and the CSS2D label overlay (HP/VP/quadrant callouts) plus the bottom-right first-angle badge; the whole subject is the HP/VP quadrant framework and first-angle fold.

nodes.label: Quadrant Picker Panel
nodes.rationale: The Step-2 'Move point P amongst Quadrants' panel: four data-quadrant I-IV buttons with a controller-stamped aria-pressed, each carrying a plain-words aria-label for its room definition.

nodes.label: Fold Actions Panel
nodes.rationale: The Step-4 reversible fold trigger (Fold HP down / Unfold back to 3D + done badge); a drag on the rotate-locked flat answer sheet fires a qv-lock-cue shake + focus ring on the Unfold button ('unfold to orbit').

nodes.label: Point P Controls
nodes.rationale: A native Module-2 #controls group (Distance from HP / VP slider-plus-field pairs in mm), not a separate dock; revealed by progressive disclosure only while the point is on stage and routed through simController.commit().

nodes.label: First-Angle Symbol Badge
nodes.rationale: The SP 46:2003 first-angle badge (#fa-symbol, truncated-cone glyph) fades in bottom-right when a step sets showSymbol (step 5, The Standard); decorative confirmation, kept aria-hidden.

nodes.label: Compare Workbench
nodes.rationale: Expanding Compare opens a true 50/50 split (ADR-037): the wizard collapses, the live 3D viewport takes the left pane, the 2D orthographic drawing the right, and the four point drivers re-parent into a docked workbench rail. Built standalone in the topic's own architecture, NOT via engine config keys (Points is off engine.js, ADR-033); the single-WebGL-canvas invariant is kept because the right pane reuses the live 2D canvas. A remeasureAfterReflow waits a second frame so the renderer sizes to the true pane.

nodes.label: Fold Swoop
nodes.rationale: The step-5 fold swoops square-on to the orthographic answer sheet (ADR-036, overturning ADR-013's held-angle hold): driveFold forward calls swoopToAnswerSheet (engage ortho, glide front-on, morph perspective to ortho on easeFold) and reverse glides back via restorePerspective; the held-angle movers and the now-unused preFoldPose/FRAME_PADDING are deleted, so the perspective camera never moves during the fold.

nodes.label: Compare 2D Drawing
nodes.rationale: main.js drawCompare() live-repaints a plain 2D canvas from the point data every rebuild (never a snapshot): a FIXED scale keyed to the 40 mm slider max so 10 mm always reads as 10 mm, the lateral PP coordinate drawn as marks sliding off a centre datum, and paper-halo view marks per ADR-016; the projector is a solid Type-B thin line (only 3D pictorial projectors stay dashed).

nodes.label: Dual-Camera Ortho Quick-Views
nodes.rationale: A second OrthographicCamera + its own OrbitControls make the Top/Front/Side quick-views TRUE orthographic reads (RULES.md 5.18); a projectionMorphK matrix morph lerps the ortho projection from the perspective one and back so the hand-off gains/loses depth smoothly. Every camera-move seam hands the live camera back to perspective first so the two cameras never fight. The rogue single-camera ADR-035 was removed.

nodes.label: Ortho Orbit Lock
nodes.rationale: A quick-view / flat read is a square-on 2D view, so orthoControls.enableRotate is false (pan + zoom stay live); a left-drag on the locked ortho camera fires a qv-lock-cue shake + focus-ring nudge on the latched chip.

nodes.label: Points Quadrant Numeral Occlusion
nodes.rationale: labelLayer.updateOcclusion raycasts camera to each I-IV numeral against the sheet FILL meshes (Line2 grids excluded since their raycast needs Raycaster.camera) and hides any occluded numeral, so numerals no longer read through the HP/VP sheets; numerals were also pushed to the far grid corners to stop clashing with P/p/p'.

nodes.label: Points Problem Library
nodes.rationale: pointProblems.js ports the K.C. John / N.D. Bhatt textbook point problems in three tiers; problemLibrary.js is a data-driven +/-0.5 mm-tolerant OR-array self-check that never auto-fills (on-plane cases keep OR-array targets so a zero-distance point grades correct in either coincident quadrant, ADR-015), loading a problem resets to defaults and routes to Step 1 so the learner dials the answer by hand.

nodes.label: Points Pipeline Migration
nodes.rationale: The topic was cut from the Module 2 skeleton onto the orchestrator pattern (ADR-033): solid generators, shapeData.js, meshAnalyzer/projectionDrawer/vertexLabeler were stripped (a dimensionless point has no edges to weld) and pointData.js + the polished hvPlanes.js/point.js were ported verbatim from the Spatial Framework sibling.

nodes.label: 3D Points Viewport
nodes.rationale: #sim-viewport shows the point P projected onto HP/VP across the four quadrants with the CSS2D label overlay, plus onboarding hints (orbit hint, contextual spotlight), a reflow note, and the fade-in first-angle badge.

nodes.label: Compare Card
nodes.rationale: The on-demand floating 'drawing sheet' (ADR-012) hosting the finished 2D orthographic drawing on a plain 2D canvas that drawCompare() live-redraws; compact/expanded via data-size, the shrink button drops back to the compact card.

nodes.label: Points Viewport Cluster
nodes.rationale: Top-left cluster: the Top/Front/Side quick-view camera chips, a (not-yet-wired) connector-line declutter toggle, and the Compare chip that unhides only once the lesson's 2D gate passes (showHP && showVP).

nodes.label: Points Guided Wizard
nodes.rationale: The 5-step rail (Quadrants / From HP / From VP / From PP / Unfold) beside a step card whose #controls block holds one static [data-ctrl] wrapper per step (quad grid, HP/VP/PP sliders, fold action), revealed one at a time by progressive disclosure.

nodes.label: Quadrant 2x2 Grid
nodes.rationale: A 2x2 I/II/III/IV button grid (data-quadrant + controller-stamped aria-pressed, the pattern proven in the Topic 2 Spatial Framework) with a live note spelling out the standard definition of the chosen room, replacing the legacy select.

nodes.label: Points Problem Library Overlay
nodes.rationale: A full-viewport focus-trapped dialog whose cards problemLibrary.js builds from pointProblems.js tiers (first-quadrant basics to four quadrants to on-plane), with a 'clears your work' confirm strip; the rAF loop pauses while it is open.

nodes.label: Active-Problem Header
nodes.rationale: A quiet paper card pinned above the step card while a textbook problem is loaded: the statement, a scaffolded 'Need a hint?' reveal (one reasoning step per click), the neutral-until-match self-check status, and an Exit-problem action that clears the framing only, never the drawing.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Introduction)
nodes.rationale: Backported the platform floating minimal scrollbars (ADR-032) to #shape-rail and #anatomy-panel: a 10px WebKit channel with a ~4px --color-border pill floating clear via a padding-box border, plus a Firefox @supports fallback, giving a 'more content below' cue.

nodes.label: Shape Rail
nodes.rationale: #shape-rail is the left sidebar where gallery.js builds the categorised list of solids (prisms, pyramids, cube, cylinder, cone) the learner picks to view.

nodes.label: Anatomy Gallery Viewport
nodes.rationale: #sim-viewport is the calm 3D anatomy gallery where main.js mounts the WebGL canvas + label overlay; introduces apex, central axis OP, generators, and base vertices with an auto-rotate turntable.

nodes.label: Anatomy Panel
nodes.rationale: #anatomy-panel renders the per-shape exposition (#anatomy-content) and hosts the show/hide display toggles and a Reset control.

nodes.label: Anatomy Display Toggles
nodes.rationale: Checkbox toggles to show/hide the Central axis (OP), Vertex labels, Generators, and Auto-rotate; the Generators toggle carries a lock glyph when hierarchy-disabled.

nodes.label: Quiet Chrome Scrollbar (Simple Positions)
nodes.rationale: Backported the platform floating minimal scrollbars (ADR-032) to #step-card and .problem-library__body: a 10px WebKit channel with a ~4px --color-border pill floating clear via a padding-box border, plus a Firefox @supports fallback.

nodes.label: Six-Step Projection Wizard
nodes.rationale: The 6-step guided wizard: Add & rest -> Position & turn -> Label vertices -> Draw top & front views -> Add side view -> Flatten to 2D, each step revealing its own action button and completion badge, with a pinned Back/Next/Reset footer.

nodes.label: Solid & Placement Controls
nodes.rationale: The dock control groups: shape select (cube/pyramids/prisms/curved), base-length and height sliders, resting-plane select (HP axis-upright vs VP axis-horizontal), distance-from-HP/VP sliders with a VP-distance-measured-to select, and a turn-about-axis slider plus Orient-to-corner toggle enforcing the simple-positions no-tilt pose model.

nodes.label: Orthographic Projection Viewport
nodes.rationale: #sim-viewport with the top-left cluster of Top/Front/Side quick-view camera chips and a connector-line declutter toggle, plus an empty-start overlay, orbit hint, spotlight, and the fade-in first-angle badge.

nodes.label: Simple Positions Problem Library
nodes.rationale: A full-viewport problem-library dialog and an active-problem header (statement, self-check, exit), the same textbook-practice component pattern as the Points topic.
